“Often carrying twigs and stones from the western mountains to fill the Eastern Sea.”
Yet the sea remains boundless.
A dead soul sinks into the deep waters, feeling the days grow colder, the nights warmer, wasting away a life in vain.
Occasionally, there are sounds—of water, of the wooden serpent colliding, of mechanisms activating. Probably some mischievous disciple here to explore. Just send him away.
But there’s a little one who seems to have found the key. Layer by layer, they reach his side, standing before him.
So young.
When did Mohist Hill gain such a promising junior? It reminds Zhang Wanshi of the afternoon when his master, Crane, tossed two porcelain dolls before him.
No, not just that afternoon—also the dawn when the mountain’s red maples bid him farewell.
It’ll get better… will it really?
Little one, can you fill that sea?
How many Jingwei birds would it take to fill that sea?
